# Safe Work Procedure (SOP) — Manual Print-Head Changeover, Press 4

**SOP No.:** SOP-PL2-PRESS4-011 · **Version:** 1.0 · **Status:** Issued for use

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Task** | Manual changeover of the print-head on Press 4, during a **planned stop** |
| **Site / asset** | Plant 2, Maharashtra — Press 4 |
| **Jurisdiction** | India / Maharashtra |
| **Hazard source (ingested)** | **JSA-2026-A14** — hazards and rated controls taken from this JSA and embedded below. This SOP does **not** re-score the risk. |
| **Target reader** | Frontline press operator |
| **Effective date** | 6 July 2026 |
| **Next review** | 6 July 2027, or on any change *(see Revision & Review block)* |
| **Grounding** | ISO 45001 clause **8.1** (operational control) & **8.1.2** (hierarchy of controls) |

> **Decision-support notice.** This SOP is decision-support for a competent workforce. It must be reviewed and signed off by a **competent person** (e.g. the Plant 2 Shift Engineer / Safety Officer) before it is used on the floor, and re-checked against the machine, JSA-2026-A14, and the manufacturer's manual on site. It is **not legal advice**. If anything in this procedure does not match the machine in front of you — **stop and ask**.

---

## 1. Purpose

To set out the **one correct, safe way** to remove the print-head from Press 4 and fit a replacement **by hand**, during a **planned stop**, so that:

- the press cannot start or move while your hands are inside it,
- you are protected from the hot and sharp print-head and from ink under pressure, and
- the press is proven safe again before it goes back into production.

A printed procedure is itself only an **administrative** control. On its own it does **not** make you safe. The controls that actually protect you — **de-energising the press, locking it out, proving zero energy, and letting the head cool** — are built into the steps below and **must be done every time**, in order.

## 2. Scope

**This SOP covers:** the manual changeover of the Press 4 print-head during a **planned stop** — from taking the press out of service, through the changeover, to proving the press safe and returning it to production.

**This SOP does NOT cover** (use the correct separate procedure / permit):

- Any changeover during a **breakdown / unplanned stop** while other faults may be present.
- **Electrical, ink-system, or mechanical repair** of the head or the press (maintenance work → maintenance PTW).
- **Confined-space, hot-work, or work-at-height** elements, if any apply → separate permit.
- Changeover on any press **other than Press 4**.
- The **risk assessment** of the task — that is held in **JSA-2026-A14**; this SOP builds the procedure around it.

## 3. Definitions

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Planned stop** | A scheduled stop where the press is brought to a controlled halt on purpose. |
| **LOTO** | Lock-Out / Tag-Out — locking every energy isolation in the OFF position and tagging it. |
| **Zero-energy state** | Proven condition where all energy (electrical, air, hydraulic, stored) is removed and the machine cannot move. |
| **PTW** | Permit to Work / isolation permit issued by the Authorised Person. |
| **Hold-point** | A point where you **must stop and confirm** a condition (e.g. head is cool) before going on. |

## 4. Roles, responsibilities & competency

Role labels only — no individual is named in this SOP.

| Role | Responsibility in this task | Required competency |
|---|---|---|
| **Authorised Person (Shift Engineer)** | Issues the isolation permit / PTW; de-energises Press 4; applies the master isolation lock; **confirms the zero-energy state**; authorises re-energisation. | Trained & authorised in machinery isolation / LOTO and PTW issue for Plant 2 presses. |
| **Press Operator** | Applies **personal lock**; carries out the changeover; runs the function-test; does not start work until zero energy is confirmed. | Trained on Press 4 operation **and** print-head changeover; LOTO-trained lock holder; inducted on JSA-2026-A14. |
| **Shift Supervisor** | Verifies the procedure is followed and the permit is in place; supports abnormal-condition decisions. | HSE-supervisory trained; familiar with this SOP and JSA-2026-A14. |

**Competency rule:** Only a trained, authorised Press Operator may carry out this changeover, and only under a live isolation permit. Training must be recorded against each role in the site training records **before** the person works alone on this task.

## 5. PPE required

PPE is the **last line** of defence and does not replace isolation and cool-down. Wear, for the whole task:

- **Cut-resistant gloves** (EN 388, high cut rating) — for guard removal and head handling *(JSA-2026-A14)*.
- **Face shield** — over safety glasses, for the unclip/fit steps *(JSA-2026-A14)*.
- **Ink-resistant / chemical gloves** — when disconnecting or handling ink lines and a wet head.
- **Safety glasses**, **safety footwear**, and **work overalls** — at all times in the press area.

Inspect all PPE before use. Do **not** start if any item is damaged, worn through, or missing.

## 6. Equipment, materials & permits required

- Valid **isolation permit / PTW** for Press 4 (from the Authorised Person).
- **Personal padlock + tag** (Press Operator) and **master isolation lock + tag** (Authorised Person); one key per lock, held by its owner only.
- Correct **replacement print-head** (verified part number) and the manufacturer's changeover tools/torque tool.
- **Voltage/energy test device** to prove dead, as specified for Press 4.
- Clean-up materials for ink (spill tray, absorbent, waste container).
- Manufacturer's print-head changeover instructions for Press 4.

---

## 7. Pre-task isolation, LOTO & energy control (do this BEFORE any changeover step)

These steps put the **higher-order controls** in place. **Do not remove any guard or touch the head until every step in Section 7 is complete.**

**7.1 — Confirm the planned stop is authorised.** Check the isolation permit / PTW for Press 4 has been issued by the Authorised Person for this task and time window.
 ⚠ *Hazard: working on a live/unauthorised machine.* ✔ *Control: no work starts without a valid PTW (administrative isolation) — JSA-2026-A14.*

**7.2 — Bring Press 4 to a controlled stop.** At the end of the run, stop the press through its normal stop sequence; do not use the emergency stop as a routine stop.
 ⚠ *Hazard: moving rollers/head, in-running nips.* ✔ *Control: controlled stop with all motion ceased before isolation.*

**7.3 — De-energise every energy source (Authorised Person).** Turn the **main electrical isolator to OFF**. Isolate **pneumatic** and **hydraulic** supplies. **Bleed off trapped air**, and **relieve ink-line / accumulator pressure** to the machine's stored-energy state.
 ⚠ *Hazard: unexpected start-up and stored energy (electrical, air, hydraulic, pressurised ink).* ✔ *Control: de-energise + release all stored energy — engineering/admin isolation, JSA-2026-A14.*

**7.4 — Lock out and tag out.** The **Authorised Person applies the master lock**; the **Press Operator applies their personal lock** to the isolation point. Attach tags naming the task and the role. Each person keeps their own key.
 ⚠ *Hazard: someone else re-energising while you work.* ✔ *Control: LOTO — the press cannot be started until every lock is removed by its owner.*

**7.5 — Prove the zero-energy state (Authorised Person confirms; Operator witnesses).** Attempt a start with the local controls to confirm the press will **not** move (try-start), then **test to confirm dead** with the energy test device and check gauges read zero.
 ⚠ *Hazard: assuming isolation worked when it did not.* ✔ *Control: zero-energy confirmation — never trust the switch, prove it dead, JSA-2026-A14.*

**7.6 — Cool-down hold-point.** After a run the print-head is **hot**. **Wait** for the head to cool to a safe touch temperature per the manufacturer's guidance before touching it. Do not force the wait.
 🛑 *HOLD-POINT — Hazard: burns from a hot head.* ✔ *Control: cool-down hold-point — do not go on until the head is safe to touch, JSA-2026-A14.*

## 8. Changeover procedure (do-this-then-that)

Only proceed if Sections 7.1–7.6 are all complete. One action per step, in order.

**8.1 — Prove the guard interlock is open, then remove the guard.** Confirm the guard interlock shows **open/safe**, then remove the guard covering the print-head.
 ⚠ *Hazard: pinch / crush; defeating the interlock.* ✔ *Control: interlock proven open before the guard comes off (engineering); wear cut-resistant gloves (PPE) — JSA-2026-A14.* **Never override or trick the interlock.**

**8.2 — Disconnect the ink lines and connectors.** Place the spill tray. Slowly disconnect the ink feed line(s) and electrical/data connector(s) from the head. Catch any residual ink.
 ⚠ *Hazard: ink contact / spray from residual pressure; slip on spilled ink.* ✔ *Control: pressure already relieved at 7.3; disconnect slowly; ink-resistant gloves + face shield (PPE); spill tray in place.*

**8.3 — Unclip and remove the old print-head.** Release the head clips/fixings and lift the head clear with both hands. Support its weight; keep fingers clear of the clip mechanism.
 ⚠ *Hazard: contact with a hot/sharp head; pinch from clips; dropped/awkward manual handling.* ✔ *Control: head confirmed cool at 7.6; cut-resistant gloves + face shield (PPE); firm two-handed hold, JSA-2026-A14.*

**8.4 — Fit the replacement print-head.** Verify the part number. Locate the new head, engage the clips/fixings, and tighten to the manufacturer's torque. Do not force it.
 ⚠ *Hazard: sharp edges; head not seated → later movement/damage.* ✔ *Control: cut-resistant gloves (PPE); fit and torque per the manufacturer's instructions; check the head is fully seated.*

**8.5 — Reconnect ink lines and connectors.** Reconnect the ink feed and electrical/data connectors correctly and fully. Check for cross-connection.
 ⚠ *Hazard: leaks / wrong connection at re-start.* ✔ *Control: reconnect per the manufacturer's instructions; visually confirm every connection is seated.*

**8.6 — Refit the guard.** Refit the guard fully and confirm it is secure. Do not leave it loose or off.
 ⚠ *Hazard: running the press with an exposed head / defeated interlock.* ✔ *Control: guard refitted and secured before any energy is restored (engineering control back in place).*

## 9. Restore to service & verification

**9.1 — Remove locks in reverse order.** Each person removes **only their own** lock and tag: **Press Operator first**, then the **Authorised Person**. Confirm all people and tools are clear of the press.
 ⚠ *Hazard: energising with someone still in the machine.* ✔ *Control: each owner removes their own lock; final walk-round confirms all clear.*

**9.2 — Re-energise under the Authorised Person's control.** The Authorised Person restores electrical, air, and hydraulic supplies and closes/authorises the permit for return to service.
 ⚠ *Hazard: uncontrolled start.* ✔ *Control: re-energisation controlled by the Authorised Person only.*

**9.3 — Function-test at low speed.** Run the press at the **lowest test speed** and watch the new head.
 ⚠ *Hazard: abnormal start / movement with a newly fitted head.* ✔ *Control: low-speed test with a stop-on-abnormal hold-point (see Section 10) — JSA-2026-A14.*

**9.4 — Verify the changeover.** Confirm: no ink leaks; print registration / quality is correct; the guard interlock functions (opening the guard stops the head); no unusual noise or heat.
 ✔ *Verification: the press is only returned to production when all four checks pass.*

**9.5 — Return to production and sign off.** Bring the press to production speed, close out the permit with the Authorised Person, and record the changeover (SOP No., date, roles) in the shift log.

## 10. Abnormal conditions & STOP rules

**STOP the task, restore isolation (re-apply locks), and call the Shift Supervisor / Authorised Person if ANY of these happen:**

- The press moves, hums, or shows power **when it should be dead** — or you **cannot prove** the zero-energy state (7.5).
- The head is **still hot** at the cool-down hold-point (7.6).
- The **guard interlock will not prove open**, or someone suggests defeating/overriding it (8.1).
- **Ink sprays or leaks**, or ink line stays pressurised after 7.3.
- A **lock or tag is missing**, or you are unsure whose lock is on the machine.
- The replacement **head or a connector is damaged**, wrong part, or will not seat/torque.
- **Anything abnormal** during the low-speed function-test — unusual noise, movement, heat, or misregistration (9.3).
- **You have any doubt.** When in doubt — stop, isolate, ask. Never improvise on a live press.
